original_title: Chiral Rh Diene NHC Complexes and Their Application in Rh-Catalyzed Cycloisomerization of Enynes
title: Putting chiral dienes and NHCs on the same rhodium
blurb: Chiral dienes and NHCs each show up constantly in transition-metal catalysis, but apparently almost nobody's put both on one Rh center at once. This makes eight neutral and four cationic Rh diene-NHC complexes to see how the two ligand types actually interact, then runs them on enyne cycloisomerization.

original_title: A Self-Marangoni-Propelled Droplet Microarray for Ultrafast Mixing and Point-of-Care Assay of Acute Myocardial Infarction Biomarkers
title: Marangoni flow does the stirring on a heart-attack biomarker chip
blurb: A droplet microarray patterned with a hydrophobic background, superhydrophilic rings, and hydrophilic cores keeps water replenishing at each droplet's edge, which sets up surface tension gradients that drive their own 3D convection. That self-stirring is what fixes the usual droplet-array problem, poor mixing and uneven signal, for point-of-care detection of acute MI biomarkers.

original_title: Through-space conductive pathways for polyoxometalate electronics
title: Polyoxometalates that conduct without touching
blurb: Assembling quasi-aromatic clusters into a 3D network creates charge-transport pathways through space rather than through bonds, turning normally insulating polyoxometalates into intrinsic molecular conductors.

original_title: Electron‐Donating Aminosilane Bridging Enables General Access to Full‐Color Aqueous Phosphorescent Nanospheres
title: One recipe for full-color glow-in-water nanoparticles
blurb: An in-situ silanization platform uses electron-donating aminosilanes as a bridge to lock organic precursors into a silica matrix, producing monodisperse, size-tunable (10-320 nm) phosphorescent nanoparticles that work in water and afterglow anywhere from blue-purple to red. The pitch is generality: one bridging chemistry instead of a bespoke recipe per color.

original_title: Alpha particle therapy in glioblastoma: emerging biomarkers, mechanisms of response, and translational opportunities.
title: The state of alpha therapy for glioblastoma
blurb: A review rounding up where alpha particle therapy for glioblastoma stands: emerging biomarkers, what's known about why some tumors respond, and where the translational opportunities are. No new data of its own, it's a survey of the field.

original_title: Extracellular vesicles in targeted drug delivery: from biological functions to surface engineering
title: Dressing up exosomes to hit the right cells
blurb: A review of surface engineering approaches for extracellular vesicles as drug carriers. The case for EVs is that they already do intercellular delivery naturally, which gives them built-in targeting and a safety profile that synthetic nanoparticles have to work a lot harder for.

original_title: Pressure‐Induced Single‐Molecule Deformation Enables 208‐Fold Photoluminescence‐Intensity Enhancement in Zero‐Dimensional Copper Iodide Hybrids
title: Squeeze a copper iodide crystal, get 208x the glow
blurb: Pressure-induced emission enhancement in metal halides has been observed for a while without anyone pinning down the molecular cause. Here it's isolated to single-molecule deformation, shown by tuning the alkyl chain length on phosphonium cations across a series of 0D copper iodide hybrids, with one packing mode delivering a 208-fold jump in photoluminescence under pressure.

original_title: Harnessing endogenous carbon monoxide for cancer-selective drug synthesis
title: Building the drug out of the tumor's own carbon monoxide
blurb: Cancer cells run hot on endogenous CO, and this turns that into a feedstock: an albumin-based system does transition-metal-mediated synthesis directly at the tumor site, engineered specifically to survive the glutathione that normally kills these catalysts fast inside cells.

original_title: Closed-loop optimization in an industrial R&D lab
title: A closed-loop reaction optimizer built to actually stay in production
blurb: An autonomous closed-loop optimization system, hardware and software, deployed inside an industrial R&D lab and built to run across multiple reaction types rather than being tuned to one process and retired as a demo.

original_title: What wonders are left to unlock using protein de novo design?
title: What wonders are left to unlock using protein de novo design?
blurb: I have a background in structure biology. We use mutations to optimise enzyme activity or even, conformational changes. I find that it's all about engineering functions because the uphill task of engineering proteins is now done. But now I am interested in understanding which frontiers are left to be scaled?
